text: Recipes assume nothing goes wrong. Real dinners share one cook, two burners, and an oven. SupperShift is a simulated Alexa Plus kitchen companion that repairs the plan when life interrupts.

This is the working application. Tonight's menu is lemon chickpeas, rice, and roast carrots. The real scheduling engine separates hands on work from passive cooking. With one cook, it finds a plan finishing at eighteen forty four, before our seven o'clock target.

Now the oven is busy for twenty minutes. SupperShift recalculates dependencies and shared resources. The new finish is nineteen oh four. It shows the consequences before applying anything. A late plan stays visibly late. It does not invent a successful deadline.
I confirm the interruption. The oven's unavailable interval now appears in the schedule. Other preparation can still happen. This is a computed plan, not a sequence of prewritten screens.

Use the salad instead. The planner compares an authored side that needs no oven. The estimate changes to eighteen thirty two. The alternative, its timing, and the steps that move are visible before I commit.
Confirmed. The task graph and timeline are now different. Changes are versioned. I can undo a plan change before further cooking progress, and stale confirmations cannot overwrite newer state.

After advancing a step on the clearly labelled demo clock, I ask: where was I? SupperShift remembers completed work, any cooking already underway, and only the next useful action. Undo cannot erase work that has already happened.
What if dinner must be ready at six twenty? The simulator reports that the computed plan misses the target. I keep the current plan. Honest constraints are more useful than confident promises.

The source includes invariant tests, generated constraint cases, and a separate open source schedule auditor. There is no paid API, no required device, and no claim of real Alexa access. This is an AI assisted, deterministic prototype with optional browser speech. SupperShift: dinner plans that survive real life.
